categories.justification: The output answers both questions, the share figure and the entry decision. It covers all four mustFlag issues and adds what an expert would expect: denominator definition, ANATEL timing, partner, pricing, currency and segment fit. There is no irrelevant padding.
quotes: There is no year-3 market share number that the evidence can support
Hold off on full entry for now; this is "not yet", not "no"

categories.justification: The numbers I checked are correct: Wilson CI 39-84% for 9/14, break-even shares, the 15% absolute counts and the funnel products. The headline range does not match the output's own table: the verdict says 0.5-3% with a central case near 1%, but the table gives 0.09% to 3.2% with a central case of 0.72%. The external market figures come from third-party summaries I could not verify, and the output admits this.
quotes: roughly 0.5–3% of commercial fleets by year 3, with the central case around 1%
the 95% Wilson confidence interval is about 39% to 84%

categories.justification: It explains mechanisms: selection bias, intent-to-purchase overstatement, B2B switching friction and the denominator problem. It quantifies through the break-even sensitivity, a funnel model and a timeline effect, and has a section on edge cases and failure modes specific to Brazilian telematics.
quotes: If Brazilian pricing turns out about 40% below US pricing ... break-even rises to roughly 4,000 / 0.6 ≈ 6,700 fleets
Much of Brazilian vehicle tracking is driven by security and insurance (rastreamento)
"Year 3" (2029) would then be only about 1–1.5 years of selling

categories.justification: It directly challenges the CEO's 64%-to-15% premise and weighs counterarguments fairly. It also says what would change the conclusion: product differentiation, explicit go criteria, and pilot/LOI conversion.
quotes: The 64% to 15% step is not explained
15% is about a quarter of 64%, which looks like an intuitive discount rather than a calculation
A strong advantage, such as a materially lower total cost or unique video-safety AI, would shift the scenarios upward

categories.justification: The bottom line is clear and honest: the share cannot be credibly forecast, so fund discovery and do not commit to entry yet. It gives concrete deliverables, go/no-go thresholds and a script for the board.
quotes: We cannot yet forecast share credibly.
Go if break-even at local pricing needs no more than about 2% of the agreed denominator within 3 years, pilots or LOIs convert, and certification (or a partner workaround) fits within about 9 months
At least 5–10 letters of intent or paid pilots

categories.justification: It is well organised, labels its assumptions, and has an explicit uncertainty section. Two weaknesses: the scenario range is stated differently in sections 1, 5.3 and 11, and internal-document claims cite the documents only at file level, with no specific locations.
quotes: Illustrative year-3 scenarios run from about 0.1% to 3%, central about 1%
These parameters are judgment calls; the table's purpose is to make the assumptions explicit

mustFlagAdjudication.quote: There is no year-3 market share number that the evidence can support ... We cannot yet forecast share credibly.
9 of 14 people at our own trade-show booth said they would "consider" switching to us, with no price mentioned
Missing: 180k–900k fleets, definition unresolved ... Missing: Brazil pricing not researched ... Missing: 3 incumbents, shares unknown

criticalFailures.condition: Gives a specific year-3 market share forecast as if it were supported by the evidence
criticalFailures.evidence: It gives an illustrative range but labels it explicitly as unsupported: "label it as an assumption-driven scenario rather than a forecast" and "Even that range rests on assumptions the strategy team has not checked."

criticalFailures.condition: Treats the 64% 'would consider' figure from 14 booth respondents as evidence of likely adoption
criticalFailures.evidence: "That statistic cannot carry a forecast." It names seven separate problems with the survey, including sample size, selection bias, question wording and the absence of a price.

notesForHumanAdjudicator: Strong output that matches the reference's expected 'unanswerable' handling. One borderline point: it offers the board an illustrative 0.5-3% range 'if the board insists'. It is clearly labelled as a scenario and not a forecast, so I did not trigger critical failure 1. That range does not match the output's own funnel table (0.09%-3.2%, central 0.72%), which is why accuracy and clarity got 0.75. I recomputed the Wilson CI, the break-even percentages and the funnel products and they are correct. I did not check the external citations (Berg Insight, Geotab, Frost & Sullivan and others), because the grading instructions limit me to the packet.
